[EFFECT]
When a given hour falls on a public holiday (value = 1 rather than 0), the model predicts **lower** bike demand — the contribution drops from a near-zero or slightly positive value on normal days to clearly negative values on holidays. The effect is a clear **step-down** at the transition from non-holiday to holiday: no gradual change, just a single downward shift. The size of the drop varies across hours but can reach quite large negative values in log space (as low as around −1.0 or more), meaning the predicted number of rentals can be cut substantially compared to the same hour on a regular day.

[IMPORTANCE]
Holiday is the **least important feature** in the entire model, ranking **9th out of 9**, with an importance score of only 0.012 — roughly 70 times smaller than the top feature (hour of day). In practice, knowing whether it is a holiday adds very little to the prediction compared to knowing the time of day, the year, temperature, or day of the week.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Since holidays reliably suppress predicted demand, there is little operational need to stock extra bikes or schedule additional staff on public holidays — if anything, slightly reduced availability and staffing on those days may be warranted, while focusing resources on peak weekday commuter hours where the model's most important drivers (hour of day, temperature) are pointing to high demand.
